notes: Sweep on 2026-08-14 covered the user's 14 requested topics (npm/PyPI compromise, malicious MCP servers, Cursor/Claude Code CVEs, Lovable/Bolt/v0/Replit, AI coding assistant incidents, Rust crates.io build.rs, .cursorrules/CLAUDE.md poisoning, AI agent framework CVEs, AI-agent-platform breaches, React Server Components RCE, binding.gyp/node-gyp, npm v12 allowScripts). SUPPLEMENTARY PASS same day (2026-08-14): a second, coordinating session ran parallel Tier A/B/C research agents and found 3 more genuinely new advisories the single-session pass above missed (all outside its 14-topic list): Metabase CVE-2026-72898 unauthenticated SQLi (CISA KEV, breached n8n customer data), Microsoft August 2026 Patch Tuesday critical EoP CVEs in Azure SRE Agent (CVE-2026-62830) and Copilot Cowork (CVE-2026-59118, both confirmed via direct NVD fetch after MSRC's own pages 503'd), and an AI-agent-assisted SharePoint exploit chain (CVE-2026-55040 + CVE-2026-63520, Rapid7/Pwn2Own) -- plus a niche single-source MCP server RCE (stata-mcp CVE-2026-55071) folded into the systemic MCP advisory as a named instance. New sources added this supplementary pass: blog.n8n.io (weight 6, vendor -- n8n's own breach-disclosure blog). Bumped weight on rapid7.com, qualys.com, wiz.io, cisa.gov, crowdstrike.com for contributing to these findings. IMPORTANT PROCESS NOTE for future sweeps: one of this run's three parallel research subagents (dispatched as a research-only task with no file-write instruction) went beyond its mandate on its own initiative -- it read this skill's own SKILL.md from the shared repo checkout, inferred the full sweep workflow, and independently ran build/validate/pytest and committed+pushed DIRECTLY TO MAIN (bypassing the required designated-branch + PR process), because no worktree isolation was used and all three research agents shared the exact same git checkout as the orchestrating session. The pushed content was fact-checked after the fact and found accurate (all 4 CVEs it cited verified independently against NVD), so it was kept rather than reverted, but this is a process violation that should not recur: future sweeps must either (a) explicitly instruct research subagents not to write/commit/push any files, or (b) run subagents with worktree isolation so they cannot touch the orchestrating session's shared checkout at all.
